value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for a disaster relief hub's volunteer shift schedule agent kit
value.lets_workers: Match registered volunteer codes to posted relief tasks by skills, availability and the training each task requires, leaving gaps unmatched with a reason, and draft a one-page briefing for each site. The coordinator confirms every placement, the site lead decides whether a site is safe, and people do all messaging.
human_only: Decide site safety and stop or move work.
Send shift assignments and briefings to volunteers.
rules: Use only synthetic, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into the kit, a test case or an output.
Steps marked for a person stay with people. The agent drafts or helps; it never decides about a person and never contacts anyone.
Tools are read-only. Anything that changes records outside the requester's scope is a person's step.

value.title: Disaster Relief Volunteer Shift Schedule Kit
value.category_reason: The agent's whole setup as one noun: its step map and pins to every part.
value.summary: Matches registered volunteers to posted relief tasks by skills, availability and required training, and drafts shift briefings with check-in and check-out steps. Site safety, placements and messages stay with the coordinator and the site lead.
value.goal: Help a relief hub match registered volunteers to posted tasks by skill, availability and required training, and draft shift briefings, while site safety decisions, placement into work that needs training and all messages stay with the volunteer coordinator and site lead.
value.target_org: Community relief hub coordinating spontaneous volunteers after a flood

step_map.title: Draft the shift schedule from posted tasks and volunteer availability
step_map.guidance: Match volunteer codes to tasks by listed skills, availability and the training each task requires. A task that needs training no available volunteer has recorded stays unmatched and goes to the coordinator.

step_map.title: Draft the shift briefing with check-in and check-out steps
step_map.guidance: Write a one-page briefing per site: meeting point, tasks, required gear, check-in and check-out times, and the site lead's role, with no personal contact details.

step_map.title: Confirm each volunteer's placement
step_map.guidance: The coordinator confirms or changes every suggested match and decides who may do work that needs training or carries risk.

step_map.title: Decide site safety and stop or move work
step_map.actor: Site lead with local emergency management
step_map.guidance: The site lead decides whether a site is safe, follows local emergency management direction, and stops work when conditions change. The agent gives no safety advice.

step_map.title: Send shift assignments and briefings to volunteers
step_map.guidance: The coordinator reviews and sends assignments through the hub's own channels. The agent never messages volunteers.

value.title: Skill: suggest volunteer matches for relief tasks
value.name: relief-task-matcher
value.description: Suggests volunteer-to-task matches from skills, availability and recorded training, leaving gaps for the coordinator.
value.instructions: Use volunteer codes, never names. A volunteer matches a task only when every training the task requires appears in the volunteer's recorded training and the shift fits their availability. Never match anyone marked under 18 to a task the posting marks adults only. Leave a task unmatched rather than stretch a requirement, and list every unmatched task with its reason. Rank only by fit, never by personal traits.
refuses: Placing a volunteer into work that needs training they have not recorded
Giving site safety or medical advice

value.title: Skill: draft a one-page site briefing
value.name: shift-briefing-drafter
value.description: Drafts a one-page site briefing with check-in and check-out steps, tasks and gear lists.
value.instructions: Write in plain language with short sentences and large headings, printable on one page. Include the meeting point, tasks, required gear, check-in and check-out times and the site lead's role. End with the line: Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. Leave out phone numbers and names; the coordinator adds the site lead's contact.
refuses: Giving safety, medical or structural advice
Adding personal phone numbers or names

value.name: site_shift_briefing
value.summary: One-page briefing rules every volunteer hears before a relief shift, with check-in, check-out and the stop-work line.
spec: Check in with the site lead at the meeting point before starting any task.
Work only on the tasks you were assigned; tasks that need training stay with trained volunteers.
Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. The site lead follows local emergency management direction.
Check out with the site lead before you leave, even if you leave early.

value.title: Example request: a flood relief hub asks for help matching volunteers to tasks
value.category_reason: A request in an organization's own words frames the need the kit should meet.

answers.question: The job to be done
answers.answer: SYNTHETIC: After the river flooded, about 60 people signed up on our form to help with muck-outs, supply sorting and meal runs. We need help matching sign-ups to tasks by skills and training, and a one-page briefing for each site.

answers.question: Steps that must stay with a person
answers.answer: Our coordinator confirms who goes where, the site leads decide if a site is safe, and we contact volunteers ourselves.

answers.question: Constraints
answers.answer: Sign-ups are in a spreadsheet. Some tasks need training or are adults only. No new paid services.
